newsitem.title: USA: Serb mercenaries leave mass graves in Zaire -report.
newsitem.headline: Serb mercenaries leave mass graves in Zaire -report.

text.p: Serb mercenaries who terrorised the Zairean city of Kisangani this month left graves containing at least 24 corpses following their bloody campaign against anti-government rebels, Newsweek International reported.
The magazine said its correspondent in Kisangani saw some of the graves, and residents said they were filled with the bodies of victims gunned down by the mostly Serb force led by Col. Dominic Yugo.

Yugo's mercenaries were among about 300 soldiers hired by Zairean President Mobuto Sese Seko in a failed attempt to turn back advancing rebels, who eventually took Kisangani two weeks ago. The Serbs fled, after blowing up their headquarters, and their current location is not known.

Newsweek International, in its issue reaching newstands on Monday, reported that witnesses said Yugo and his group "personally killed all the victims as part of a vicious dragnet for rebel sympathisers, or, perhaps, just in sadistic sport."
In one episode on March 10, residents saw Yugo herd 15 young men into a hut, and later heard gunfire and screams.
Other witnesses said earlier that Yugo himself shot down two evangelical pastors while they held their Bibles and begged for mercy.
The fall of Kisangani after the mercenaries' reign of terror broke the hold of Mobutu, reviled by many of his own people.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) hold a fifth of Zaire, is now referred to as the city's protector.
